# Rentzu Pricing Research & Decision

> **Implementation status: DONE** (Stripe/web) **+ IN PROGRESS** (RevenueCat/native). For how to run DB migrations, configure Stripe test-mode credentials, set up RevenueCat, and manually test every scenario below, see `PRICING_IMPLEMENTATION_TESTING.md` in the repo root.

Product angle: **tax-ready bookkeeping for small landlords**, with metered **voice-to-text** capture as the differentiating paid hook. Billing is **per-unit** (Stripe).

## Freemium strategy (adopted 07/18/2026)

Give the commodity away, meter the differentiators. Free users get the full manual bookkeeping system so we maximize top-of-funnel adoption; the two things that cost us money and/or drive real value — **voice-to-text AI conversion** and **tax-ready exports** — are the paywalls.

- **Unlimited units on free** — creating/managing units and manual record entry is free.
- **Free voice taste: 3 conversions/month**, then paywall. (A small taste converts better than a hard zero — users pay for time-savings they've already felt.)
- **Tax-ready exports gated behind paid** — year-end / Schedule E export and PDF reports require a paid plan. This adds a second conversion moment at tax season so we don't bet 100% of monetization on voice.

## Confirmed pricing decision

| Plan | Monthly (per unit) | Annual (per unit) | Voice / month / unit | Tax-ready exports | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Free** | $0 | $0 | 3 (taste) | No | Unlimited units + manual entry free; drives adoption |
| **Normal** | $1.99 | ~$19.99 (~16% off) | 10 | Yes | Raised annual from earlier $9.99 to keep a healthy — not extreme — discount |
| **Pro** | ~$2.99 | ~$29 | 30 | Yes | Added a monthly option (was annual-only $25) so it mirrors Normal's ladder. Renamed from "Unlimited" (clearer, and quota isn't literally unlimited). |

Rules: free orgs get 3 voice conversions/month and cannot run tax-ready exports; exceeding voice quota or attempting a gated export blocks with a clear upgrade prompt. Show a "billed annually" toggle with the monthly-equivalent price (market standard).

## Billing model: per-unit *pricing*, account-level *entitlements* (adopted 07/18/2026)

Units are **not** independently subscribed. The **account (org) is put on a plan**, and the **price scales by the account's total unit count**. There is no per-unit cherry-picking (no "unit 1 paid, unit 2 free" within one account).

- **Price** = per-unit rate × number of units. E.g. 2 units on Normal = $1.99 × 2 = $3.98/mo. When an account goes paid, **every unit it has is billed**.
- **Entitlements are account-level** — once paid, voice quota and tax-ready exports apply to the **whole account** (all properties/units), not to specific units.
- **Voice quota:** Free = **3/month account-wide** (flat allowance, not per unit). Paid = quota × units (Normal 10×units, Pro 30×units).
- **Tax-ready exports** are never sold per unit — a Schedule E is per *property*, and a partial (single-unit) export would be a broken tax document. Any paid plan unlocks exports for the entire account.

Rationale for account-level (vs true per-unit subscriptions): tax reporting is per-property so partial exports are useless; a mixed free/paid account would need two voice quota pools (ambiguous which one an entry draws from); per-unit proration/cherry-picking explodes billing complexity for a fast rollout. Matches REI Hub, which bills total portfolio unit count and does not let you cherry-pick units.

### Changing unit count on a paid account
Paid accounts can **add or remove properties/units anytime** — we never block portfolio growth. Because price = per-unit rate × count:
- Adding a unit **increments the Stripe subscription quantity** (prorated for the current period) and **raises the voice allotment** (Normal +10/mo, Pro +30/mo).
- Removing a unit decrements quantity (proration credit) and lowers the allotment.
- Show a **confirmation of the price change before committing** (e.g. "Adding this unit changes your plan to $X.98/mo, prorated $Y today").
- Free accounts add/remove units at no cost (units are the commodity).

### Voice conversion length cap
Voice must be capped per conversion — transcription (Whisper) + model cost scales with audio duration, so unbounded recordings are a cost/abuse risk.
- **Cap: 30 seconds per conversion** (a bookkeeping note is typically 5–10s; 30s covers multi-record entries).
- Enforce in **two layers**: (1) **client** auto-stops recording at 30s with a clear "max length reached" message; (2) **server** rejects audio over the size/duration threshold *before* transcribing (defense in depth against direct API abuse).
- Current gap: only a client-side *minimum* (1.2s) exists in `useVoiceRecorder.ts`; there is **no maximum** on client or server (`routers/voice.py` transcribes any uploaded audio). This must be added.

### Rationale
- **Per-unit is market-validated** — REI Hub (closest comp) uses per-unit tiers.
- **Freemium via feature-gating, not unit caps** — unlimited free units maximizes signups (Landlord Studio/Baselane prove free tiers drive growth); we monetize the two differentiators instead.
- **Voice is the only truly unique lever** — no competitor meters or offers voice-to-text; metering also caps Whisper transcription cost. But a *2/month taste* hooks users rather than walling them out.
- **Second paywall at tax season** — gating exports captures the annual "I need my taxes done" moment so monetization doesn't depend on voice alone.
- Original annual $9.99/unit was a 58% discount vs monthly; market standard is ~20% (REI Hub, Stessa, TurboTenant). Raised to ~$19.99 to avoid leaving money on the table.
- Watch item: a *flat* per-unit rate gets expensive for 10+ unit landlords vs competitors' declining/volume tiers. Revisit volume discounts if targeting larger portfolios.

### Future promotions (post-launch)
- **Volume discount for larger portfolios — decided, deferred to post-launch.** Launch with a **flat $1.99/unit**; later add a graduated break where **units 5+ drop to ~$1.50/unit** (first 4 stay at $1.99). Rationale: our ICP is small landlords (1–4 units) who already have no cheaper alternative ($1.99 vs REI Hub's ~$3 effective at 3 units), so we protect full price through that sweet spot and only discount where REI Hub becomes competitive (~10 units, where its effective per-unit hits ~$1.50). Chose the 5+ threshold over discounting every extra unit (which would leak margin on the 2–4 unit core). Deferred to keep the launch on a clean "quantity × flat rate" Stripe model; graduated tiers (Stripe supports them) layer on later without changing the core account-level model.
- Other promo levers: promo codes / limited-time discounts once an account passes a unit threshold.
- The **"Pro"** name (renamed from "Unlimited") leaves room for a future higher tier if needed.

## Competitor pricing snapshot (captured live via Chrome DevTools MCP, July 2026)

| App | Model | Free tier | Paid pricing | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **REI Hub** (closest comp) | Per-unit tiers, annual | No (14-day trial) | 3u $9, 10u $15, 20u $27, unltd $48 /mo billed annually (monthly ≈1.65×) | Tax-ready: Schedule E, P&L, depreciation, fixed assets. No voice. |
| **Stessa** | Flat, annual | Yes (unlimited properties) | Manage $12/mo, Pro $28/mo (billed annually) | Banking + bookkeeping; 5 receipt scans/mo free; 1–7 eSign/mo |
| **Landlord Studio** | Unit-slider + flat | Free ≤3 units | Pro $12/mo ($144/yr), Pro Plus $28/mo ($336/yr) | Rent collection, screening, reporting |
| **TurboTenant** | Flat, annual | Yes (unlimited listings) | Essentials $12.42/mo ($149/yr), Pro $16.58/mo ($199/yr) | Listing/screening-first |
| **Baselane** | Free banking + bookkeeping tiers | Yes ($0) | Bookkeeping up to ~$20/mo at 30+ properties | Fintech/banking-first; FDIC up to $3M |

Common patterns across the market: annual billing framed prominently with ~20% discount; a free tier is near-universal; nobody meters voice-to-text.

## Additional decisions (07/18/2026)

### Bank-feed integration (Plaid / Yodlee) — deferred post-launch
Plaid and Yodlee are third-party **bank-data aggregators**: they let an app securely connect to a user's bank/credit-card accounts and auto-import transactions, so the user doesn't have to type/speak every entry. Considered as a possible v2 differentiator.
- **Decision: not building now.** Voice input + manual entry are enough for MVP/fast-rollout; bank-feed integration adds real cost (per-connection fees from Plaid/Yodlee), compliance/security surface (bank credentials, read access to full transaction history), and reconciliation UX complexity (matching imported transactions to properties/units) that isn't justified pre-launch.
- Revisit post-launch if landlords ask for it or if voice/manual entry proves to be a retention bottleneck. Plaid is the more common/cheaper starting point of the two if pursued later.

### Mortgage transaction category — added 07/18/2026
Most landlords pay mortgage principal + interest, and **only the interest portion is tax-deductible** (Schedule E line 12); principal is equity-building, not a deductible expense. The category system previously had a single `interest` code that was (a) not clearly separated from principal and (b) **missing from the Schedule E PDF labels**, so it silently fell into "Other Expenses."
- **Decision:** keep `interest` for mortgage/loan interest (deductible) and add a new `mortgage` category for principal payments (non-deductible, cash-flow only — excluded from deductible-expense totals and from Schedule E's deduction lines, but still visible in the transaction list/summary).
- **Status: implemented this session** (see Implementation status below) — schema, backend validation/aliasing, voice-extraction prompt, and all three frontend category pickers/labels/report groupings were updated in lockstep.

### Native mobile billing (RevenueCat) — decided 07/25/2026
Stripe Checkout (opened via `Linking.openURL` in a system browser) is **not App Store/Play Store compliant** for a native app: both platforms require their own in-app-purchase system (Apple StoreKit / Google Play Billing) for digital subscriptions that unlock in-app features — our paid plan unlocks voice quota + tax exports, which is squarely "digital content used within the app" under Apple Guideline 3.1.1 and Google Play's Billing policy. "Google Pay" is a card-wallet payment method, not a substitute for Play Billing, and does not solve this.

**Decision: use RevenueCat**, a service that wraps StoreKit + Play Billing behind one SDK/webhook, rather than building native StoreKit and Play Billing integrations by hand.
- **Why RevenueCat over hand-rolled native IAP:** one shared SDK/API instead of two separate native codebases (receipt validation, restore purchases, renewal handling per platform); one webhook to reconcile subscription state instead of two. Tradeoff: RevenueCat takes a small fee on top of Apple/Google's cut (free up to $2.5k/month tracked revenue, ~1% after) in exchange for materially less engineering time.
- **Apple/Google's cut is unavoidable either way** — 30% year 1, 15% after a subscriber's 12th month, on top of whatever billing integration is used. This is separate from (and unrelated to) the RevenueCat fee.
- **Stripe remains the web billing path** — unchanged; only iOS/Android switch to RevenueCat. `create_checkout_session` now rejects starting a new Stripe subscription for an org already billed via RevenueCat (and vice versa isn't applicable since RevenueCat entitlements are applied directly, not requested by the backend).
- **Same account-level entitlement model applies** — RevenueCat doesn't change the "account is on a plan, price scales by unit count" design; it's still the org's `plan` that's set from whichever provider (Stripe or RevenueCat) currently reports it as paid, exposed via a new `billing_provider` column (`'stripe'` | `'revenuecat'`) on `organization_billing`.
- **App user id = organization id.** The app configures `Purchases.configure({ appUserID: organizationId })`, so RevenueCat webhook events resolve straight back to the org with no separate alias/mapping table.
- **Entitlements, not raw product ids, drive plan mapping** — each paid plan (Normal, Pro) maps to one RevenueCat "entitlement" (`REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_NORMAL` / `REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_PRO` env vars), and the backend picks the highest-ranked plan among a customer's active entitlements. This matches how RevenueCat is meant to be used (entitlements as the app-facing abstraction over store-specific product ids) and keeps App Store/Play Store product identifiers out of app code.
- **Two sync paths, one core function:** (1) a client-driven sync (`POST /billing/revenuecat/sync`) called right after a purchase/restore completes on-device, so the UI updates immediately without waiting on webhook delivery; (2) a server-to-server webhook (`POST /billing/revenuecat/webhook`, authenticated via a shared `Authorization` header secret) that is the authoritative source for renewals, cancellations, and expirations that happen while the app isn't open. Both funnel through `apply_revenuecat_entitlement_state` in `services/billing.py` so there's exactly one place that turns "active entitlements" into plan/quota state.
- **Cancellation vs. expiration handled distinctly** — a `CANCELLATION` event only stops auto-renew (the entitlement, and thus the plan, stays active until the paid period actually ends); an `EXPIRATION` event is what actually downgrades the org to Free. This mirrors how Stripe's `cancel_at_period_end` already worked.
- **react-native-purchases requires a custom dev client / EAS build — it does not work in Expo Go.** This repo currently runs as a plain Expo managed app; see `PRICING_IMPLEMENTATION_TESTING.md` for the dev-client build step needed before this can be tested on-device.
- **Not solved by this change:** actually creating the App Store/Play Store subscription products, App Store Connect/Play Console setup, and Apple/Google developer account enrollment are manual dashboard steps outside this codebase (see "Needs from you" below).

## Implementation status (07/18/2026)

**All items below are implemented and validated** (Python syntax/import checks + `npx tsc --noEmit` passed; see `PRICING_IMPLEMENTATION_TESTING.md` for how to run/verify end-to-end with real Stripe test-mode credentials):

- ✅ Backend plan tiers (Free/Normal/Pro) + monthly/yearly Stripe prices — `services/billing.py`, `schemas/billing.py`, `routers/billing.py` (new `/billing/plans` endpoint).
- ✅ Account-level entitlements, per-unit pricing, no cherry-picking — `calculate_unit_counts`, `get_billing_overview`, `create_checkout_session` all bill `total_units` once an account is on a paid plan.
- ✅ Voice quota tracking + enforcement (`get_voice_quota_status`/`consume_voice_quota` in `services/billing.py`; wired into `routers/voice.py`'s `/transcribe` endpoint, returns HTTP 402 when exhausted).
- ✅ 30-second voice recording cap, enforced **both** client-side (`app/src/hooks/useVoiceRecorder.ts` auto-stop timer) and server-side (`services/audio_convert.py`'s `probe_audio_duration_seconds` + a size-based fallback estimate when `ffprobe` isn't installed; `routers/voice.py` returns HTTP 400 if exceeded).
- ✅ Tax-ready export gating — `services/billing.py`'s `exports_allowed_for_org`; `routers/reports.py` returns HTTP 402 for free-plan orgs on both `/reports/schedule-e` and `/reports/property-expense`; `app/src/screens/TaxReadyScreen.tsx` shows an "Upgrade required" alert on that 402.
- ✅ Frontend billing UI updated for tiers — `app/App.tsx`'s Account tab Plan card now has plan (Normal/Pro) + interval (Monthly/Yearly) selectors, shows voice-quota usage, and calls the updated `app/src/services/billing.ts` (`listBillingPlans`, `openBillingCheckout(orgId, plan, interval)`).
- ✅ Mortgage vs. interest category split (see above) across schema (`financial_records_schema.sql` + `schema_updates/2026-07-18-financial-record-add-mortgage-category.sql`), backend (`schemas/financial_record.py`, `routers/voice.py`, `services/reports.py`, `services/properties.py`), and frontend (`RecordFormScreen.tsx`, `HomeScreen.tsx`, `TaxReadyScreen.tsx`).
- ✅ New DB migration for billing columns: `schema_updates/2026-07-18-organization-billing-plan-tiers.sql`.
- ✅ `.env.example` documents all new env vars (4 Stripe price IDs, pricing/quota cents/counts, `RENTZU_MAX_VOICE_SECONDS`).

**Not yet done / explicitly deferred:**
- Plaid/Yodlee bank-feed integration (deferred post-launch, see above).
- Volume discount for 5+ units (deferred post-launch, see "Future promotions" above) — no code changes needed until then.
- `STRIPE_CHECKOUT_SUCCESS_URL`/`CANCEL_URL`/`CUSTOMER_PORTAL_RETURN_URL` still point at placeholder `https://example.com/...` URLs — replace with a real deep link/hosted page before shipping to production.
- No automated tests exist for any of this (repo has no test suite) — all validation is manual; see `PRICING_IMPLEMENTATION_TESTING.md` for the full manual test-scenario checklist and how to plug in Stripe test-mode credentials.

## Native mobile billing (RevenueCat) implementation status (07/25/2026)

**Code implemented and validated** (Python syntax checks + `npx tsc --noEmit` passed; not yet runtime-tested — see "Needs from you" below and `PRICING_IMPLEMENTATION_TESTING.md`):

- ✅ `billing_provider` (`'stripe'` | `'revenuecat'`) + `revenuecat_app_user_id`/`revenuecat_entitlement_id`/`revenuecat_product_id`/`revenuecat_store` columns on `organization_billing` — `models/organization_billing.py`, migration `schema_updates/2026-07-25-organization-billing-add-revenuecat.sql`.
- ✅ New `revenuecat_events` audit table + `RevenueCatEvent` model, mirroring the existing `billing_events`/`BillingEvent` pattern, with event-id de-duplication (RevenueCat may redeliver the same webhook event).
- ✅ `plan_catalog()` now exposes `revenuecat_entitlement_id` per plan (read from `REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_NORMAL`/`REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_PRO`), returned by `GET /billing/plans`.
- ✅ `apply_revenuecat_entitlement_state` (single core function used by both sync paths) + `sync_revenuecat_entitlement` (client-driven) + `handle_revenuecat_webhook_event` (server-to-server, cancellation vs. expiration handled distinctly) in `services/billing.py`.
- ✅ New endpoints — `POST /billing/revenuecat/sync` (authenticated, called by the app after purchase/restore) and `POST /billing/revenuecat/webhook` (shared-secret authenticated via `verify_revenuecat_webhook_authorization`) in `routers/billing.py`.
- ✅ `get_billing_overview` now returns `billing_provider` + `revenuecat_configured`, and gates `checkout_available`/`customer_portal_available` off once an org is RevenueCat-billed; `recommended_action` becomes `'manage_in_app_store'` for RevenueCat-billed paid accounts. `create_checkout_session` rejects starting Stripe checkout for an org already on RevenueCat.
- ✅ App: `app/src/services/revenueCat.ts` (lazy-requires `react-native-purchases` so import never throws on web/Expo Go), `app/src/services/billing.ts`'s `syncRevenueCatEntitlement`, and `App.tsx`'s Plan card now branches on `Platform.OS` — web keeps Stripe Checkout, iOS/Android use RevenueCat purchase/restore, with a "Manage subscription" action that deep-links to the OS's native subscription settings for paid RevenueCat accounts.
- ✅ `react-native-purchases` added to `app/package.json` and installed.
- ✅ `.env.example` (server) documents `REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_NORMAL`/`REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_PRO`/`REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTHORIZATION`; new `app/.env.example` documents the client-side `EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_IOS_SDK_KEY`/`EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_ANDROID_SDK_KEY`.

**Needs from you before this can be tested or shipped (logged, no defaults assumed):**
1. **Apple Developer Program + Google Play Console enrollment** (if not already done) — required to create subscription products at all.
2. **App Store Connect subscription products** for Normal/Pro × monthly/yearly (4 products), and the equivalent **Google Play Console subscription products**.
3. **A RevenueCat account/project** with those store products attached to two entitlements (`normal_access`-style identifiers of your choosing), plus its **public SDK keys** (iOS + Android) and a **webhook shared secret** you configure in both RevenueCat's dashboard and our `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTHORIZATION` env var.
4. **A custom Expo dev client / EAS build** — `react-native-purchases` cannot run inside Expo Go, so on-device testing requires building a dev client (`eas build --profile development`) at minimum once these credentials exist.
5. **Decide the two RevenueCat entitlement identifier strings** (e.g. `normal_access`, `pro_access`) — used to configure both the RevenueCat dashboard and the `REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_NORMAL`/`_PRO` env vars.
